title: 2026_PMC13100012_Coverage_and_associated_factors_of_inactivated_polio_vaccine_up
ehr_evidence: The current study was conducted based on the most recent Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) data of 20 Sub-Saharan African countries.
summary: Secondary data analysis assessing inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) coverage and determinants among children aged 12–23 months across 20 Sub-Saharan African countries using pooled DHS survey data.
key_findings: Maternal age 20–35 years (AOR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.00, 1.18) and >35 years (AOR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.11, 1.34) were positively associated with IPV uptake.
Maternal education at primary (AOR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.23, 1.37) and secondary+ levels (AOR = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.76, 1.99) increased odds.
Rich household wealth showed an inverse association (AOR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.89).

ANC visits 1–3 (AOR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.72, 2.01) and ≥4 (AOR = 2.51, 95% CI: 2.33, 2.70), health facility delivery (AOR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.77, 1.97), and PNC (AOR = 1.73, 95% CI: 1.65, 1.82) were significant positive determinants.
Urban residence (AOR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.17, 1.31) and high community women's literacy (AOR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.54, 1.83) were associated with higher uptake.
Regional disparities were observed, with Southern Africa showing the highest odds compared to Central Africa (AOR = 8.41, 95% CI: 7.08, 9.99).
study_design: cross-sectional secondary data analysis with multilevel logistic regression
population: children aged 12–23 months and their mothers in 20 Sub-Saharan African countries (weighted n=43,564)
exposure_domain: socio-demographic factors, maternal healthcare utilization, community-level characteristics, and geographic region
limitations: reliance on verbal reports and vaccination cards may introduce recall bias
limited data on health system factors
potential time lag between data collection and publication
